# Ten car-following measures on NGSIM: descriptive statistics

*Generated by `tools/ngsim_ssm1d.py`; do not edit by hand. Aggregates only; the data are the FHWA NGSIM trajectories (modified CC BY 2.0, credit FHWA and NGSIM; US-101 and I-80 only). **Descriptive: no outcome (conflict, crash, braking) is used, so nothing here validates or ranks a measure.***

## What was computed

* Data: 6 recordings of NGSIM; 8,238,546 follower-leader pair-frames with a positive clear gap of at most 200 m; the statistics are on every 10th frame (1 s) of a pair, 823,852 rows.
* Pairs: the data set's `Preceding Vehicle` column (the vehicle ahead in the same lane); positions are smoothed with a causal 5-frame mean first, the speed is the backward difference of the smoothed position, the acceleration the causal 5-frame mean of its backward difference (decision fixed before the run; the data set's own acceleration column is not used). Gap = centre distance along the follower's heading minus half the sum of the lengths; speeds and accelerations (derived as just described) are projected on that heading; the jerk is the central difference of the acceleration along the consecutive frames of the pair (rows without a neighbouring frame are dropped; the jerk, hence TTC3, is noisy).
* Parameters of the stories, **fixed before the run** (the 2025 paper gives no values; assumptions, not data): reaction time 1 s, leader deceleration 6 m/s2, follower deceleration 6 m/s2. Printed-form differences are as in `docs/ssm1d_notes.md` (the code uses the derived forms). A second set (1.5 s, 4, 4 m/s2) shows the sensitivity.
* Defined values: time measures (TTC1, TTC2, TTC3, TTCD): a positive root within 10 s; DRAC, MDRAC: closing pairs (positive, finite); PSD, MPSD, DCIA: finite; SDI is 0 or 1 for every row. The polygon indicators (TTC, TAdv, T2, TG) use the horizon 10 s with rectangular bodies of the follower's heading and constant velocity.
* The reference column here is the data set's own `Spacing` (front centre to front centre) minus the length of the leader, which equals our clear gap by construction of the definition; the check below tests the units and the reader. This report is the **descriptive step only** (no outcome).

* Check of the gap: our clear gap minus the data set's own headway column (823,655 rows): median -0.010 m, 5th to 95th percentile -0.547 to 0.462 m, largest absolute 109.544 m.
* Check of the polygon: of 135,487 rows with TTC1 within the horizon, the polygon TTC is defined in 105,874; where both are defined the largest absolute difference is 8.429147 s. TTC1 sees only the distance and the speeds along the heading, the polygon also the lateral separation and the lateral velocities of the bodies, so the two differ where the vehicles move sideways relative to each other or pass side by side (the polygon then has no TTC).
* State of the polygon over all sampled rows: collision course (A) 12.9 %, crossing course (B) 59.6 %, no overlap within the horizon (C) 27.5 %.

## Spearman rank correlation with the polygon indicators

Pairwise complete cases of the defined values (`n` below 200 is not reported). Time measures, TAdv, T2, TG, the lateral margin and beta are larger when safer; DRAC, MDRAC, DCIA, SDI and the required braking are larger when more critical, so expect negative signs between the two families. Descriptive: a high correlation says two readings order the same pairs alike, not that either is right.

Note on the signed margin beta: it uses the prediction-error scales of this data set (`docs/diamond_NGSIM.md`, tau = 2 s; sigma_delta = 1.1588 s, sigma_eps = 3.2553 m), taken from the NGSIM sites that have unhindered vehicles under the 15 m rule (Lankershim and Peachtree; US-101 and I-80 have none, because of dense traffic) and applied to the freeway pairs, so they are not scales of freeway traffic. only its ordering is used here.
